summaryZh: de Guglielmo 实验室研究成瘾神经回路，关注物质滥用与依赖相关不良行为的分子和细胞机制。页面列出光遗传学、药理学、生理学及动物模型等研究兴趣，但未明确这些方法的实际采用。
researchQuestions: 哪些分子和细胞机制导致与药物滥用和依赖相关的不良行为后果？

evidence.quote: Welcome to the de Guglielmo Lab! Overview Our program focuses on the neural circuits of addiction, with an emphasis on critical molecular and cellular mechanisms that are responsible for adverse behavioral outcomes that are associated with substance abuse and dependence. The de Guglielmo Lab is located in the department of Psychiatry at the UC San Diego School of Medicine and is part of the Preclinical Addiction Research Consortium (PARC) of UC San Diego Interests Drug addiction, Neuropeptides, Dependence, Optogenetics, Pharmacology, Physiology, Neuronal Ensembles, Animal Models, Cellular and Behavioral Pharmacology In the News Opioid Dependence Found to Permanently Change Brains of Rats Science Daily January 24, 2020 Approximately one-quarter of patients who are prescribed opioids for chronic pain misuse them, with five to ten percent developing an opioid use disorder or addiction. In a new study, researchers found that opioid dependence produced permanent changes in the brains of rats. Article Publication Cellular Atlas of Amygdala Reveals New Treatment Target for Cocaine Addiction University of California News October 12, 2023 Researchers at the University of California San Diego School of Medicine and the Salk Institute for Biological Studies have created a unique, cell-by-cell atlas of the amygdala, a small structure deep within the brain that plays a crucial role in controlling emotional responses to drugs. Article Publication UCSD’s Center for Medicinal Cannabis Research Awards Grants for Five Novel Studies UC San Diego Health Press Release October 10, 2019 The Center for Medicinal Cannabis Research (CMCR) at the University of California San Diego School of Medicine, the nation’s oldest research center for scientific inquiry into the safety and efficacy of cannabis, has announced $3 million in research grants to explore new applications of cannabis for a number of novel medical applications. Article Advancing AUD Research: Our Biobank Highlighted in eNeuro eNeuro News January 22, 2026 Dr. Giordano de Guglielmo and Dr. Michelle Doyle highlight the Preclinical Alcohol Biobank in eNeuro ’s “Beyond the Paper” interview. Built from 700+ genetically diverse rats, this FAIR-compliant resource links behavioral data, a DSM-5–aligned addiction index, and genome sequencing to advance alcohol use disorder research. Learn more at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40940169/ Full Interview eNeuro Investigating the Neural Circuits of Addiction
